original_question: Let Delta be a vector distribution on a manifold M, and call it singular transitive when any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves of Delta. Does singular transitivity force the symmetry group of Delta, meaning the diffeomorphisms Phi of M with Phi_* Delta = Delta, to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?
target_in_paper: Section V, "Symmetries of vector distributions," specifically the paper’s stated open question: "Is it true that singular transitivity of the distribution implies that its symmetry group is a finite dimensional Lie group?" The term "singular curve" used there is supplied earlier in Section III via the endpoint map. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact formulation: it has the right object (a vector distribution Δ on a manifold M), the paper’s definition of singular transitivity (any two points connected by a concatenation of singular curves), the right symmetry notion (diffeomorphisms Φ with Φ_*Δ=Δ), and the exact mathematical conclusion being asked about (whether the symmetry group must be a finite-dimensional Lie group). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should state that one is considering a smooth vector distribution Δ⊂TM on a smooth manifold M; Section V imposes no extra rank, analyticity, genericity, or bracket-generating hypothesis, so none should be added. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The phrase "singular curve" should be defined explicitly. In Section III, singular curves are defined as critical points of the endpoint map on the Hilbert manifold of admissible paths starting at a fixed point q0. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

For self-containment, the question should also say what admissible paths are, e.g. absolutely continuous curves tangent to Δ (the paper earlier discusses admissible paths for distributions/sub-Riemannian structures before defining singular curves through the endpoint map). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

It is slightly sharper to name the symmetry group explicitly as Sym(Δ)={Φ∈Diff(M): Φ_*Δ=Δ}, since Section V asks about the full symmetry group of the distribution. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
refined_question: Let Δ⊂TM be a smooth vector distribution on a smooth manifold M. Call an admissible curve singular if it is a critical point of the endpoint map for Δ, and call Δ singular transitive if any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves. Must the full symmetry group Sym(Δ):={Φ∈Diff(M) : Φ_*Δ=Δ} be a finite-dimensional Lie group? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: The draft is targeting Section V exactly, not a broader neighboring problem. Section V defines a symmetry of a distribution by Φ_*Δ=Δ, introduces the term "singular transitive" for distributions whose points can be joined by concatenations of singular curves, and then asks precisely whether singular transitivity forces the symmetry group to be a finite-dimensional Lie group. The only paper-critical notion left implicit in the draft is the meaning of "singular curve," which the paper defines earlier in Section III as a critical point of the endpoint map on the Hilbert manifold of admissible paths. Because Section V does not add rank, codimension, genericity, analyticity, or bracket-generating assumptions, the refined question should remain exactly at that level of generality. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
